title: Emrys and the Extraction
premise: Edmund Hartwell, a disgraced intelligence analyst hiding in a remote safe house with his estranged daughter Wren and two fellow witnesses, discovers the property has been listed online — interior photos revealing documents he buried years ago. The listing is bait set by Vesper, an assassin contracted by three governments who each want the Hartwell file destroyed before a whistleblower tribunal. As the group races to smuggle the truth to a journalist's extraction flight at dawn, Edmund learns the leak came from inside their found family, forcing him to choose between survival and the inheritance of guilt he owes his daughter. The flight leaves at dawn; Edmund stays behind to hold the line, but Wren carries the truth out, ending the cycle of silence.
about_author: Noor Nakamura is a former risk analyst turned novelist who writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped in extraordinary machinery. They live between Osaka and Lisbon, where they collect train timetables and unfinished crossword puzzles.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Edmund, sleepless as always, finds the safe house on a real estate site — twelve photos of rooms only four people alive have seen. POV: Edmund. Beat: dread crystallizes into certainty that invisibility was always an illusion.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Edmund gathers the household: Wren, ex-interpreter Mirela, and young hacker Dev. He hides the listing, testing whether any of them already knew. POV: Edmund. Beat: paranoia dressed up as paternal care.

chapters.title: Wren Counts the Doors
chapters.summary: Wren, who memorizes exits the way other teens memorize song lyrics, notices her father lied about the photos. POV: Wren. Beat: resentment — she inherited his fear without his explanations.

chapters.title: Vesper Books a Viewing
chapters.summary: The assassin Vesper poses as a cash buyer, studying the agent's feed for faces in reflections. POV: Vesper. Beat: cold professionalism laced with an unsettling respect for whoever hid so well.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Edmund's last agency job, the Hartwell file, and the incident that broke him across three governments' secrets. POV: Edmund. Beat: shame explained at last — the price he paid to survive.

chapters.title: The Open House
chapters.summary: A stranger tours the house while the family pretends to be caretakers. Mirela spots the wire under his coat. POV: Mirela. Beat: terror managed through translation — she narrates danger in three languages.

chapters.title: Runners and Stayers
chapters.summary: The group votes: run now or retrieve the backup drive hidden in the house before Vesper returns. POV: Edmund. Beat: leadership he never wanted, fracturing the fragile family.

chapters.title: Dev's Confession
chapters.summary: Dev admits he posted the house on a darknet forum months ago to prove it existed — the listing grew from his bragging. POV: Dev. Beat: guilt of the youngest, begging not to be sent away.

chapters.title: The Drive Beneath the Floor
chapters.summary: Retrieval sequence: the drive is under the nursery floorboards, guarded by Edmund's own traps. Wren disarms them because she helped build them as a child. POV: Wren. Beat: inheritance made literal.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Edmund reaches journalist Ilse Brandt, who offers seats on a dawn extraction flight from a decommissioned airfield — if they bring the file uncorrupted. POV: Edmund. Beat: hope that feels like another trap.

chapters.title: Mirela's Price
chapters.summary: Mirela reveals she's been reporting to one government to protect her brother held in detention; Vesper knows. POV: Mirela. Beat: the terrible arithmetic of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Roadblock
chapters.summary: Convoy to the airfield is stopped by a 'routine' checkpoint that isn't. Dev spoofs their plates; they pass with minutes to spare. POV: Dev. Beat: competence as redemption.

chapters.title: What Vesper Wants
chapters.summary: Vesper intercepts them off-road — not to kill, but to offer Edmund erasure of his record in exchange for the drive. POV: Vesper. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Edmund refuses; gunfire scatters the group into the marshland. Mirela is wounded covering Wren. POV: Edmund. Beat: the cost of principle, paid in blood.

chapters.title: Marshlight
chapters.summary: Wren drags Mirela through reeds while Edmund draws pursuit away alone. POV: Wren. Beat: the child becoming the protector.

chapters.title: The Turncoat Question
chapters.summary: Regrouping in a chapel ruin, the survivors confront who leaked the listing — evidence points to Mirela, then to someone else entirely. POV: Mirela. Beat: betrayal reframed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ilse's Terms
chapters.summary: Ilse reveals the flight can take only two passengers plus the drive; the governments are closing in. POV: Edmund. Beat: Sophie's choice with a boarding pass.

chapters.title: Dawn Approach
chapters.summary: They move on the airfield as fog lifts; Vesper is already there, having traded employers mid-contract. POV: Vesper. Beat: the assassin's own inheritance — a life spent as currency.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Climax: standoff on the runway. Edmund offers himself and the truth together; Vesper, seeing Wren board, lets the plane go and takes Edmund instead of the kill. POV: alternating Edmund/Wren. Beat: love outranking survival.

chapters.title: Tribunal Morning
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the Hartwell file detonates across three governments; Wren testifies via video from safety. POV: Wren. Beat: grief braided with vindication.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Edmund, detained but alive, receives a letter from Vesper — a single photo of the safe house, empty, unlisted. POV: Edmund. Beat: peace purchased at full price.

chapters.title: Found Family, Forward Address
chapters.summary: Wren, Mirela, and Dev reunite in Lisbon; a new door, new locks, chosen this time. Final image: Wren sleeps through the night. POV: Wren. Beat: inheritance rewritten — vigilance passed down becomes rest finally earned.
